name: Supreme Court of Pakistan
assumptions: Heading set to 240.4 degrees, not the dossier 238.4: the OSM wing edges and the two axial star pavings measure a 2 degree turn.

No height is published. Portal top 25.5 m, towers 31 m, triangular roof 30.5 m at its front point and 43 m at its back edge were fitted to telephoto photos, with the portal width of 25.5 m from the satellite view as the only scale; expect a few metres of error.

Ground plan corrected for satellite lean of about 0.45 x height; the OSM ring stops the back of the wings at the 44 m line, but the satellite view shows them running the full length, so the satellite was followed.
Tower plan (a splayed front face about 45 degrees from the axis) inferred from photo perspective and the satellite view; the backs of the towers were not seen.
Side terraces, inner courts and their gardens are simplified from the satellite view; the inner court walls and storeys were not photographed.
Wings drawn with three storeys and 22 window bays per long side, an estimate from aerial photos.
Rear elevation is a plain window bank: no photo of the back was found.
Rear of the triangular hall is a plain marble wall to the rim height: not seen.
Marble colour, emblem detail and flag proportions are estimates from photos; the emblem is a simplified disc and balance.
Entry level 6 m above the star plaza, three equal flights: step counts are estimated.
Side forecourt pads are plain; the small guard building at the south of the frontage is left out.
